messages:
rachael: Quick async — small API-contract clarification before tonight's canary. Question: how should stop sequences, max_tokens, temperature/top_p, and logprobs interact (streaming and non-streaming)? I have a few concrete examples below, want to lock behavior so we don't regress.

vikram: can you paste a minimal repro payload so we all mean the same thing?

rachael: pasted example: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1-small",
  "prompt": "Translate:\nHello",
  "max_tokens": 3,  // strict generate limit
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.9,
  "top_p": 0.5,
  "logprobs": 5,
  "stream": true
}
```
Expected behavior I'm assuming: streaming should emit tokens until either (a) a stop sequence is observed in the decoded output (should stop immediately and not emit the stop text), OR (b) max_tokens tokens have been emitted. When stop causes an early end, we still return logprobs for the final emitted token.

ben: current runtime notes: we stop when a token boundary decodes to include the stop substring. Important: because tokenizer may emit tokens that include the stop text as part of a token, we only detect stops after decoding tokens, not inside byte runs. We don't emit the stop content but we might emit the token that contains the stop substring if we don't post-process. I think we need to clarify spec: do we require post-decode substring trimming?

olga: another contract point: order of sampling ops (temperature vs top_p). My expectation (and what SDKs/docs should declare): apply temperature scaling to logits, softmax, then apply nucleus/top_p truncation & renormalize, then sample. If someone's implementation does top_p first then temperature it produces different dist. We should pick and document.

vikram: agreed. Also: what happens when top_p is low (0.5) and temperature is high (0.9)? should still be valid and consistent.

rachael: on logprobs + streaming: if stream=true we currently send incremental events with token text and optional logprobs. If a stop triggers that requires trimming part of the last token's decoded string, the logprob we reported may not match the trimmed output. Proposal: spec says servers must either (1) only return logprobs for fully retained tokens (drop any token where we later trim part of the decoded token), OR (2) perform substring-level postprocessing before emitting streaming chunks so emitted token pieces always have accurate logprobs. I'm leaning to (1) since (2) is tricky for partial-token alignment. Thoughts?

ben: (1) seems safer. Add a test: generate a token that decodes to "abc\n\n" (stop inside token) with logprobs and assert we don't return that token + logprob when stop applies. I'll add it to generator-tests.

olga: also backward-compat note: default temperature changed in the last release (was 1.0, now 0.8 in hosted). This causes small sampling diffs for customers who omit temp/top_p. We need a docs callout and a migration note for Dedicated/Private users. Can we add a deprecation/compat flag?

infra-bot: heads up: canary deploy for runtime v1.9 starts 23:00 UTC, 50% traffic. Please avoid breaking contract changes during window. :warning:

vikaem (vikram): @ben can you add the unit + end-to-end tests you mentioned? also add a short note in the API spec doc about sampling op order and the logprob streaming rule.

ben: on it. PR link incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128 (draft) — adding tests for: stop-vs-max-tokens, streaming-logprob-trim, sampling-order smoke.

rachael: thanks. Quick checklist for merge: 
- ben: add tests + small change to streaming (drop final token when stop trims it)
- docs: olga please add migration note + sampling-order paragraph
- infra: don't flip defaults during canary

olga: noted, will draft docs PR.

vikram: small question for API: do we want to preserve the old default behavior behind a header like `X-Compat-Sampling: legacy` so enterprise can opt in? might be useful.

rachael: yes let's design an opt-in header. Ben — add behaviour toggle feature-flag behind runtime config but keep default as current hosted behavior; olga will document header.

ben: ack. I'll implement flag and tests.

rachael: thanks all — if no objections I'll merge the tests tomorrow morning and coordinate with infra to avoid canary window. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: noted — will pause canary progression if we detect new runtime binary with sampling-default changes until engineering confirms.

vikram: no objections from me.

olga: :+1: closing loop, thanks!
